Basic Usage

Learn the fundamentals of using RoselineMCP to analyze and improve your C# code.

Overview

RoselineMCP provides four main tools:

  1. AnalyzeSolution - Analyze entire solutions
  2. ListDiagnostics - Get detailed project diagnostics
  3. ApplyFixes - Apply automated code fixes
  4. CreatePatch - Generate diff patches

Quick Examples

Analyzing a Solution

# Analyze a solution file
mcp call analyzeSolution '{
  "pathOrGit": "/path/to/MySolution.sln"
}'

Listing Project Diagnostics

# List diagnostics for a specific project
mcp call listDiagnostics '{
  "project": "MyProject.Core"
}'

Applying Fixes

# Preview fixes without applying
mcp call applyFixes '{
  "project": "MyProject.Core",
  "ids": ["CS0168", "IDE0005"],
  "previewOnly": true
}'

Creating Patches

# Generate a diff patch
mcp call createPatch '{
  "before": "old code",
  "after": "new code",
  "fileName": "Example.cs"
}'

Understanding Diagnostics

Diagnostic IDs

RoselineMCP supports various diagnostic ID patterns:

  • CS#### - C# compiler warnings and errors
  • IDE#### - IDE suggestions and refactorings
  • RCS#### - Roslynator analyzer diagnostics
  • SA#### - StyleCop analyzer rules
  • CA#### - Code Analysis rules

Severity Levels

Diagnostics are categorized by severity:

  • Error - Code that won't compile
  • Warning - Potential issues or bad practices
  • Info - Suggestions for improvement
  • Hidden - Silent diagnostics (usually for IDE features)

Filtering Options

By Severity

Filter diagnostics by minimum severity:

{
  "severity": "warning"  // Shows warnings and errors only
}

By Project Pattern

Include or exclude projects by name pattern:

{
  "include": "Core",     // Only projects containing "Core"
  "exclude": "Test"      // Exclude projects containing "Test"
}

By Diagnostic ID

Focus on specific diagnostic types:

{
  "ids": ["CS0168", "CS0219", "IDE0005"]
}

By File Pattern

Filter by file paths:

{
  "files": ["**/Controllers/**", "**/Services/**"]
}

Working with Results

Solution Analysis Response

{
  "solution": "MySolution.sln",
  "projects": 5,
  "diagnosticSummary": {
    "error": 2,
    "warning": 45,
    "info": 12
  },
  "topDiagnostics": [...]
}

Diagnostic Details

Each diagnostic includes:

{
  "project": "MyProject",
  "file": "Program.cs",
  "line": 42,
  "column": 12,
  "id": "CS0168",
  "severity": "warning",
  "message": "The variable 'x' is declared but never used"
}

Fix Application Response

{
  "project": "MyProject",
  "fixesApplied": 12,
  "filesChanged": ["File1.cs", "File2.cs"],
  "patch": "--- a/File1.cs\n+++ b/File1.cs\n...",
  "appliedFixers": [...]
}

Best Practices

1. Start with Analysis

Always analyze first to understand the scope:

# Get an overview
analyzeSolution --severity warning --maxDiagnostics 50

2. Use Preview Mode

Preview fixes before applying:

# Preview without changing files
applyFixes --previewOnly true

3. Filter Strategically

Focus on what matters:

# Only production code errors
analyzeSolution --exclude "Test" --severity error

4. Apply Fixes Incrementally

Fix issues in batches:

# Fix one type at a time
applyFixes --ids ["CS0168"]  # Unused variables
applyFixes --ids ["IDE0005"]  # Unnecessary usings

5. Document Changes

Generate patches for review:

# Create a patch for documentation
createPatch --fileName "Changes.cs"

Integration Examples

With Claude Desktop

Once configured, you can ask Claude:

  • "Analyze my solution at /path/to/solution.sln"
  • "List all unused variable warnings in MyProject"
  • "Fix all StyleCop issues in the Core project"
  • "Show me what would change if we fix all IDE suggestions"

In Scripts

Automate analysis in your build pipeline:

#!/bin/bash
# analyze.sh

SOLUTION="/path/to/solution.sln"
RESULT=$(mcp call analyzeSolution "{\"pathOrGit\": \"$SOLUTION\"}")

if [[ $RESULT == *"\"error\": 0"* ]]; then
  echo "✅ No errors found"
else
  echo "❌ Errors detected"
  exit 1
fi

In CI/CD

Add to your GitHub Actions:

- name: Analyze Code
  run: |
    dotnet run --project RoselineMCP \
      analyzeSolution --path ${{ github.workspace }}/Solution.sln \
      --severity error

Common Workflows

Code Review Preparation

  1. Analyze the solution
  2. List fixable diagnostics
  3. Apply style fixes
  4. Generate patch for review

Technical Debt Reduction

  1. Analyze with all severities
  2. Group by diagnostic ID
  3. Fix most common issues first
  4. Track progress over time

Pre-commit Cleanup

  1. List diagnostics in changed files
  2. Apply automated fixes
  3. Review the patch
  4. Commit the improvements

Troubleshooting

No Diagnostics Found

  • Verify the project builds successfully
  • Check if analyzers are installed
  • Try without filters first

Fixes Not Applied

  • Ensure the diagnostic ID is fixable
  • Check file permissions
  • Verify no compilation errors

Performance Issues

  • Use maxDiagnostics to limit results
  • Filter by specific projects
  • Process in smaller batches
